ASML exits 2023 with clear demand strength and resilient profitability, while near-term revenue is set up for a seasonal digestion phase. Q4 net sales of €7.2B and gross margin of 51.4% reinforce pricing power and favorable mix (notably €2.3B of EUV revenue on 10 systems). Installed Base Management at €1.6B adds a steadier, higher-visibility stream that helps dampen lithography cyclicality. The key forward indicator—net system bookings of €9.2B—exceeded Q4 sales, implying backlog expansion and supporting the view that leading-edge investment remains intact.

Relative to peers, ASML stands out on margin structure and bookings-to-sales (>1), consistent with its near-monopoly positioning in EUV. TSM’s continued heavy capex guidance underscores that customers are still funding leading-edge roadmaps, which is a constructive read-through for ASML’s medium-term tool demand even if quarterly shipments fluctuate.

Historically, revenue re-accelerated into Q4 after a softer mid-year cadence, and EPS rebounded to €5.21 after drifting down through 2023—both supportive for sentiment. The main trading signal to watch is the contrast between strong bookings/backlog and Q1’24 sales guidance (€5.0–€5.5B), which flags near-term volatility and potential multiple compression if macro rates stay high (policy rate 5.33%, 10Y ~4.44%). Bull case: backlog-driven visibility + stable margins. Bear case: rate-sensitive valuation + seasonal/industry digestion.

ASML’s 2024-Q1 prints as a “high-quality cyclical pause.” Revenue and earnings clearly decelerated versus 2023: total sales were €5.3B with net system sales €4.0B, and EPS fell to €3.11 from the ~€4.8–€5.0 range last year. The key near-term trading signal is bookings vs sales: €3.6B net system bookings came in below €4.0B system sales, implying softer order flow and limiting upside until bookings re-accelerate.

Offsetting that, ASML’s profitability and visibility remain standout. Gross margin held at 51%, supported by a large Installed Base Management stream (€1.3B) and meaningful EUV contribution (€1.8B; 12 EUV systems). The ~€38B backlog is the dominant bullish anchor, reducing demand cliff risk even as customers digest capex. Versus peers (proxy: TSMC), ASML screens structurally stronger on margin and forward visibility; it also captures a meaningful share of industry investment, though it looks weaker on absolute liquidity (cash €5.4B down QoQ).

Macro is mixed for multiples: inflation is near 3% but policy rates remain restrictive (FFR ~5.33%, 10Y ~4.16%), which can cap valuation expansion until growth re-accelerates. Net: tactically neutral-to-cautious near term (bookings/earnings momentum), but strategically constructive given backlog, EUV leadership, and service resilience.

ASML’s 2025-Q3 prints as a “transition” quarter rather than a demand break. Revenue (€7.5B) is below the FY25 run-rate implied by ~€32.5B guidance, but the guided Q4 step-up (€9.2–€9.8B) is the key near-term signal: it points to delivery timing and mix normalization, not structural weakness. Profitability remains a standout versus typical semi-cap equipment: 51.6% gross margin and ~28% net margin show strong pricing power and a resilient installed base stream (€2.0B, ~27% of sales), with management reiterating a path to 56–60% gross margin by 2030.

Peer context is supportive. However, bookings (€5.4B) are only ~72% of quarterly sales—healthy, but not a clear re-acceleration—so the stock likely trades on Q4 execution and 2026 visibility.

Macro is also mildly restrictive (policy rate and yields ~4.3%), which can pressure long-duration multiples even if fundamentals hold.

Trading takeaway: constructive bias if Q4 delivery ramp lands and EUV bookings stay firm; caution if China weakness starts to leak into broader backlog conversion.
